name: Assisted Chin Tuck
description: A controlled neck flexion that strengthens the front of the neck — the sternocleidomastoid and deep neck flexors — by drawing the chin toward the chest.
instructions: Sit or lie down tall with your shoulders relaxed and your head in a neutral position.
Slowly tuck your chin and lower it toward your chest, moving only as far as feels comfortable.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, feeling the front of your neck work.
Return your head smoothly to the start under full control. Keep every rep slow and controlled, and never jerk the head or use heavy load on the neck.

name: Posterior Neck Isometric
description: A static neck hold that builds stability in the cervical flexors and extensors by pressing gently and holding without movement.
instructions: Sit or stand tall and place a hand against your head in the direction you will press.
Press your head gently into your hand and hold the position without letting your head actually move.
Hold steadily for the prescribed time, breathing slowly and keeping the effort light.
Release the pressure gradually and relax. Keep every rep slow and controlled, and never jerk the head or use heavy load on the neck.

name: Weighted Lying Side Lifting Head (with head harnes
description: A controlled side-bend of the neck that works the sternocleidomastoid and scalenes by lowering the ear toward the shoulder. Performed with a weight plate.
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders down and relaxed.
Slowly lower one ear toward that same shoulder without lifting the shoulder up to meet it.
Pause for a moment when you feel a gentle stretch and contraction along the side of your neck.
Bring your head smoothly back to center under control, then repeat to the other side. Keep every rep slow and controlled, and never jerk the head or use heavy load on the neck.
